tagline: An Army freight road through the long gallery of the Fremont.
intro: From Wellington, south of Price, the road heads northeast on Soldier Creek Road into Nine Mile Canyon, down a flat bottom of grazing and farm ground between craggy buff walls topped with pinyon, juniper and sage. At the far end the backway runs through Gate Canyon to Myton.

Buffalo Soldiers of the 9th Cavalry built the road in 1886 to tie Fort Duchesne to the railroad at Price, and until about 1905 most of the stage, mail and freight traffic into the Uinta Basin came this way. The Fremont were here long before, farming corn and squash on the canyon floor.

moments.title: Telegraph poles
moments.text: The Army ran telegraph poles up the canyon around 1886, Civil War surplus, and they went on to carry the Basin's telephone line from 1907 to 1917.

moments.title: Rock art panels
moments.text: Along the road and up the side canyons the walls carry Fremont petroglyphs and pictographs and later Ute hunters on horseback, rock art more concentrated here than anywhere else in North America.

moments.title: Harper
moments.text: A stagecoach stop that grew into a long scatter of ranches with a hotel and a school, a ghost by the early 1920s, whose precinct never cast more than 72 votes.
